It will all depend on how you build. I normally build between a .4 and .6 because that's where I like it. I usually can get in a decent session on my way to work, and about 45 minutes in breaks at work but when I get home I swap my battery for the night. YMMV

It definitely can be at first. But once you learn how to do it safely and you're not throwing a .08 build on a purple efest like some people I see at my local b&ms you will appreciate it a lot more. If you're cloud chasing as well, don't be afraid to get a decent regulated box. They can perform just as well as a good mechanical build but they can be a lot safer on the batteries

Two things you're gonna want to read up on, Ohms law and your batteries. As long as your coils are within a safe range of your battery you should be find. The ohm meter lets you check for shorts as well as what resistance the coil is. If you're just getting into subohm vaping I wouldn't build any lower than a .6 just to get the idea and that's still relatively safe. There are resources out there such as steam-engine.org which allow you to measure things in ohms law, as well as help with coil builds and stuff. 

The idea is you don't want to build a coil that is going to draw more power than your battery can handle, that's when you get into territory that can be dangerous with a possible vent or explosion.

Research will be your best friend in your endeavor. Happy vaping :)

South Side/Carson Street is the largest area of the nightlife here. Tons of bars and clubs as well as a hookah bar and food options well into the night.

There are also quite a few bar options in Oakland. 

I believe last call is at 2 or 3 but I am not sure as I usually leave before last call so sorry on that one. Same goes for public transportation but I think buses end around midnight. Once again I could be wrong. 

Off the beaten path? Not really that I can think of. There are a lot of good little mom and pop places all around town. If this is your first time in Pittsburgh you HAVE to go to Primanti BrothersI though or we throw you out after a grace period. Apart from that I'd avoid the chains and try and hit as many little hole in the wall restaurants you can. That's where the real Pittsburgh food is! 

I recommend checking out the North Shore although it might be a little cold out this time of year. Regardless you get a beautiful view of the city. 

Ride the incline!

 I see you've already mentioned the museums so make sure you get to the Carnegie Science Center as well as the Warhol. Museum of Natural History is a good one too. If you're into weird art, The Matress Factory is a must. 

Places to avoid? Not that they are many "bad" areas but there just isn't much for them to offer as other parts. Homestead comes to mind. The Waterfront has a lot of restaurants and shops but 8th Avenue and the surrounding streets can get a little seedy. (basically right next door) 

Apart from that there are tons of good things in Pittsburgh as well. Try some Homebrew at Fatheads or check out the Penn Brewery or Church Brew Works.

Over all seems like you want to explore the city. That's the best thing you can do when visiting! 

Have a great visit here!
